title: AI For Life
summary: Making practical AI easier to learn, one walkthrough at a time.
problem: New AI users need a clear starting point, understandable terminology, and examples that connect tools to real work.
approach: A student club resource hub brings together tool walkthroughs, business use cases, a searchable glossary, prompts, and a beginner learning roadmap.
demonstrates: Organizing technical information into an approachable learning experience.
limit: An educational resource; tool details need ongoing review as products change.

title: Text From Sheet
summary: Texts a spreadsheet of contacts from a person's own phone number: personalized, paced, and built with guardrails.
problem: A non-technical family member needed to text a few hundred people who know him from his own number. Bulk-texting services start around $25 a month and require carrier registration; sending by hand is slow and error-prone.
approach: A Python rules engine normalizes phone numbers and enforces consent, opt-out and do-not-text lists, duplicate removal, and sensitive-data blocking. An Android (Termux) sender paces texts about one a minute between 8am and 6pm after one typed approval, logs every send so it can resume, and runs from one-tap home-screen buttons, including a file picker for Excel lists. A no-install web app offers a review-each-text version. Extras: STOP-reply scanning, birthday automation with a one-time approval, and picture mode.
demonstrates: Turning a real user's request into requirements, building controls against misuse and compliance mistakes, and verifying the result with 150+ automated tests and a build-versus-buy comparison.
limit: Tests use simulated senders; not yet field-tested on a phone. Delivery is not confirmed, picture texts need one tap per person (an Android limit), and all sample data is fictional.

title: Client Inquiry Pipeline
status: Public source · working demo with fake data
summary: A serverless AWS pipeline that saves quote-request inquiries as structured records, so questions like "which products do people ask about most?" are answered with SQL instead of by digging through an inbox.
problem: A website form that only sends an email makes basic questions hard to answer: which products draw the most interest, and how many inquiries came in this week.
approach: A static form on S3 and CloudFront posts to an API Gateway endpoint. A Python Lambda function validates each inquiry and saves it as a JSON file in a private S3 bucket, and Athena runs SQL over those files. The backend is also defined as code with AWS SAM, and 12 unit tests plus a template check run on every push through GitHub Actions.
skills: AWS (S3, Lambda, API Gateway, Athena, CloudFront)
demonstrates: Designing a small data pipeline around a business question, applying least-privilege access and server-side validation, and finding and fixing a bug by building the backend twice (hand-built versus as code).
limit: A learning project built on fake data only; the analytics numbers come from 101 generated inquiries and are not market findings. The API has no authentication, and it is throttled.
captions: The request-a-quote form, served over HTTPS (fake sample data).
Athena counting inquiries by product, on 101 synthetic records.

title: Insurance website
summary: A web application for an insurance advisory business.
problem: An advisory business needs an organized digital presence that visitors can navigate and understand.
approach: A React and TypeScript website uses reusable interface components and structured routing.
demonstrates: Building a business-facing web interface with reusable components.
limit: Source is private. A public website address has not been added to this portfolio.

title: Options research lab
summary: A reproducible foundation for studying simulated options execution.
problem: Research results are hard to trust without explicit costs, valid data, and reproducible experiment records.
approach: A Python toolkit validates input data, replays simulated execution, records experiment metadata, and tests accounting and data integrity using synthetic fixtures.
demonstrates: Building auditable research infrastructure and documenting the limits of evidence.
limit: No trading edge has been established. This is offline research, with no live-order code.

title: Mass Email Sender
summary: A desktop workflow for personalized spreadsheet-based email campaigns.
problem: Repeated communication needs personalization, campaign tracking, and a clear review step before sending.
approach: A desktop application organizes templates, spreadsheet imports, business-specific campaigns, previews, and scheduled sends.
demonstrates: Turning a repetitive business process into a guided, reviewable workflow.
limit: A local application; client lists, messages, and account data are not part of this portfolio.

title: Woodworking showcase
summary: A product and storytelling website for handcrafted bookshelves.
problem: A craft business needs a way to explain its story and present its products clearly.
approach: A React website separates editable content from layout, with product, gallery, and story sections.
demonstrates: Structuring a marketing website so content can be maintained in one place.
limit: Business details and photography remain to be completed before launch.
